source.title: Pharmacodynamics of Cefazolin in the Presence of Normal and Impaired Renal Function
source.design: single-dose intramuscular cefazolin study across renal function, with a three-volunteer within-subject probenecid re-exposure

governing_source_execution.summary-evaluation-appraisal-protocol-v4: read and applied as governing SEA file
governing_source_execution.unslop.skill.md: retrieved from File Library and applied to prose artifacts

protocol_version_note: The governing SEA filename is labeled v4, while its internal heading identifies Integrated Compact v3. The project precedence names the v4 filename as authoritative, so that file governed this run.
extraction_limitations: The abstract reports 12 subjects, while the methods describe five healthy volunteers plus nine renal-failure patients. Table 1 has 14 non-probenecid observation rows and lists C.L. twice at different creatinine clearances. The source does not reconcile this accounting.
The study used a single 500 mg intramuscular dose in a small sample. It did not study repeated dosing, infected patients receiving treatment, or patient-centered clinical outcomes.
Demographic reporting is sparse. The article does not provide enough age, sex, or other covariate detail to judge subgroup generalizability.
The discussion cites reference 18 for biliary levels, but the bibliography ends at reference 17. The missing citation cannot be reconstructed from the supplied source without external verification.
No external current-practice or bibliographic verification was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review because no independent human verification step is represented.
